lesson.title: Who Takes the Deep Lob?
lesson.hook: A deep lob goes over you. Your partner is already deeper. Both of you chasing it would leave nobody organising the next ball.
lesson.liveIntro: A deep lob goes over you. Your partner is already deeper. Both of you chasing it would leave nobody organising the next ball.

dlbA.name: What does this next ball call for?
dlbA.sit: Your pair has reorganised. Read this contact before trying to finish.
dlbA.q: What does this next ball call for?
opts: Use controlled depth through the middle

lines.A: You give the ball room and prepare together for another reply.
lines.B: It lands here, but the smaller target leaves less margin. Keep covering.

dlbA.take: Call early. Cover while your partner retrieves.
dlbA.payoff: Call early. Cover while your partner retrieves.
dlbA.principle: Call early. Cover while your partner retrieves.
dlbA.why: Here the deeper partner has the shorter route. An early call assigns the ball and the uncovered half. Turn to run; don’t backpedal under a ball already beyond comfortable overhead range.

pro.label: Cayer · Even the pros get lobbed
pro.moment: Louis Cayer warns that crowding the net invites lobs—even for professionals. Being closer feels aggressive, but it can leave the next ball behind you before you have room to turn.
pro.read: Your next point: this lob has already beaten the net player. Call early, let the partner with room retrieve it, and cover the court together.

drill.name: Rehearse as a pair
drill.how: Start one up, one back. Feed a deep lob. Require an early ownership call, a switch and a recovery shot, then play out the next two balls.
